sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2021. Front matter/Introduction pp. 1-17.
sources.note: Leipon listed in Table 0.1 (6.5 contact hours, 3 days) and under Eastern Manus in the subgrouping figure; Leipon is not one of the eight sketches; nothing on Leipon stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Sketch 6: Loniu. In Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands (LLM Special Issue 2021).
sources.note: Leipon mentioned only for a shared possessive-vowel-rounding pattern (p.383) and Loniu-Bipi-Leipon lexical innovations (sec. 6.7.1); no Leipon phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised edition). Asia-Pacific Linguistics Open Access Monographs A-PL 008. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Leipon cited for bilabial/alveolar trills (brudr, bri-n), irregular low-vowel raising (minde-w, time-w, kitah) and PAdm *nika reflexes; nothing on Leipon stress.

sources.citation: Hamel, Patricia J. 1994. A grammar and lexicon of Loniu, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-103. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Grammar of neighbouring Loniu; Leipon/Pityilu occurs only as the placename 'picilu' in the lexicon; nothing on Leipon.
